results.title: Casio to Release MR-G Crafted in Blue Sapphire Crystal
results.description: Featuring Multi-Component Structure with Screwless Design TOKYO , Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Casio Computer Co., Ltd. announces the release of a new MR-G timepiece, adding to the flagship collection of the G-SHOCK brand of shock-resistant watches. The new MRG-D5000 features a screwless, multi-component structure and a bezel rendered entirely in blue sapphire crystal. The watch will be available in a limited edition of only 20 pieces worldwide. MRG-D5000 Driven by the philosophy, "Breaking Ground," the MR-G collection has consistently defied convention in watchmaking. Since its launch in 1996, MR-G has drawn on fine processing technologies and master craftsmanship to create timepieces that combine toughness and beauty. The MRG-D5000 is the first G-SHOCK timepiece to achieve a shock-resistant structure using components made with blue sapphire crystal. The proprietary MR-G Multi-Guard Structure employs a bezel and case composed of multiple separate components assembled without the screws that can cause sapphire crystal to crack. Casio analyzed the force transmitted to the sapphire crystal when the watch is subjected to impact and developed a shock-resistant structure optimized for protecting that material. The resulting case and bezel combine tough construction with aesthetic beauty. Blue sapphire crystal is also set into the screw-lock case back, which is engraved with an individual serial number marking each of the 20 limited-edition timepieces. The module incorporates Gallium Tough Solar for outstanding durability under intense light and highly efficient charging. Casio also announces the release of two additional timepieces designed with blue sapphire crystal. The MRG-B5000SA is an MR-G timepiece featuring two-carat, facet-cut blue sapphire crystals at the top and bottom of the case. The bezel is made with a super-hard alloy, while blue arc ion plating (AIP) is applied to both the case and bezel. The GMW-B5000SB, a full-metal G-SHOCK, presents blue sapphire crystal stones set at four points on the front of the bezel. MRG-D5000／MRG-B5000SA／GMW-B5000SB

results.title: TIER IV joins Arm Total Design for Physical AI to accelerate ready-to-use Autoware solutions through Open AD Kit
results.description: TOKYO , Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TIER IV , the pioneering force behind Autoware, open-source software for autonomous driving, today announced that it has joined Arm® Total Design for Physical AI . Building on its longstanding collaboration with Arm through Open AD Kit , TIER IV aims to make Autoware more readily available across Arm-based SoCs and in-vehicle computing platforms, helping semiconductor manufacturers and OEM manufacturers accelerate the development of autonomous driving systems. Bringing open-source autonomous driving expertise to the physical AI ecosystem Arm Total Design for Physical AI brings together partners across the computing and software ecosystem to accelerate the development and deployment of physical AI, with the aim to make it easier to develop intelligent systems that operate in the physical world. As a member of Arm Total Design for Physical AI, TIER IV will contribute its expertise in open-source autonomous driving and its experience in developing Autoware-based systems. TIER IV aims to connect the Autoware ecosystem with a broader network of computing and technology partners, helping developers bring autonomous driving software to real-world applications. Building on collaboration through Open AD Kit TIER IV and Arm have a longstanding collaboration through Open AD Kit, an open framework developed within the Autoware Foundation ecosystem to simplify the development and deployment of Autoware across computing platforms. Their work brings together open-source autonomous driving software and Arm-based computing technologies, helping simplify the integration of software with hardware. The collaboration was demonstrated at CES 2026 , where Open AD Kit was showcased on Arm-based computing platforms. Building on this experience, TIER IV aims to make Autoware available in ready-to-use configurations that support development from Arm-based SoCs to in-vehicle computing platforms. "Making autonomous driving accessible requires more than open-source software. Developers also need a practical path to bring that software onto the computing platforms that power real-world systems," said Shinpei Kato, founder and CEO of TIER IV . "Our collaboration with Arm through Open AD Kit has helped bridge that gap. By joining Arm Total Design for Physical AI, we look forward to extending this work with a broader network of partners and accelerating the democratization of autonomous driving." "The path to scalable autonomy depends on making it easier for software and hardware to evolve together," said Dermot O'Driscoll, vice president of go-to-market, Physical AI, Arm . "Our work with TIER IV through Open AD Kit has already demonstrated that potential, and Arm Total Design for Physical AI gives us an opportunity to extend that collaboration across a much broader ecosystem." Advancing the democratization of autonomous driving TIER IV will continue working with Arm and other industry partners to make Autoware more accessible across computing platforms. Through Open AD Kit and the broader physical AI ecosystem, TIER IV aims to lower development barriers and enable more companies to develop and deploy autonomous driving systems. About TIER IV TIER IV stands at the forefront of deep tech innovation, pioneering Autoware , open-source software for autonomous driving. With a comprehensive suite of platforms and services built around Autoware, TIER IV provides everything from software development and vehicle procurement to operational support. Through the Autoware ecosystem, TIER IV works with partners worldwide to shape the future of intelligent vehicles with open-source software, aiming to create mobility that is safer, more sustainable, and accessible to all.
